summary: Discovery call with Celestia Biotech to understand requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood Private. Key concerns: offline updates, image signing, hardware constraints (NVLink, MIG, single-root GPU), network segmentation, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO audit evidence, and expected throughput/latency. Agreement to send architecture docs and price guidance and schedule SE deep dive.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya from Redwood, account exec, joining with Diego our SE. real quick intros?
00:07 Asha Patel: Hi Asha here, CTO at Celestia, I run platform and infra.
00:11 Leo Martin: Leo — head of infra, I'll cover the env details.
00:14 Ben Holmes: Ben, Compliance lead, will ask questions about audit and encryption.
00:18 Diego Rivera: Diego, Redwood SE, I work on private deployments and onprem air-gapped installs.
00:22 Maya Chen: Awesome. The goal today is to understand your constraints for an air-gapped on-prem deployment and what success looks like. We'll cover network, hardware, update processes, and compliance needs.
00:33 Asha Patel: High level — we have regulated data (clinical trial notes), need no egress, everything must be air-gapped, and updates go through a strict approval process. We want to evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private but leaning private onprem due to regs.
00:46 Leo Martin: Current infra: 2 racks of A100 80GB (NVLink enabled) in our co-lo, single root, not shared with other tenants. We also have some older T4s for preprocessing. We need to know supported SKUs and whether Redwood runtime supports NVLink and multi-node KV cache.
01:02 Diego Rivera: We support A100 80GB and A100S, and the runtime can leverage NVLink for model parallelism where needed; multi-node KV cache is supported with our private controller in the VPC. In air-gapped installs the controller is deployed inside the network.
01:22 Ben Holmes: For air-gapped: how do you handle updates? We cannot allow direct pull from the internet. We need signed images, offline bundles, and verifiable hashes — and ideally HSM for key signing.
01:34 Diego Rivera: Yes, understood. We provide an offline update workflow: we generate signed artifacts (we can use customer-provided keys via HSM/KMS or Redwood-managed signing in exceptional cases), provide SHA256 hashes, and a transfer package that you import via secure media.
01:48 Asha Patel: Who holds the signing keys typically? We need customer-held keys.
01:52 Diego Rivera: We prefer customer-managed keys for regulated envs. We integrate with HSMs that expose PKCS#11, or cloud KMS exports in a wrapped form for on-prem.
02:04 Leo Martin: So the workflow is: Redwood releases image bundle, we validate signatures with our HSM, then install during maintenance window, correct?
02:11 Diego Rivera: Exactly. We also support airgapped telemetry where logs are stored locally and pulled out only as packaged artifacts if you permit.
02:20 Ben Holmes: About audit logs — we need immutable logs, RBAC traces, and exportable evidence for SOC2 and ISO.
02:26 Maya Chen: Our Private offering includes audit log collection, RBAC integrated with your SSO (SAML/Okta), and we can provide export snapshots for audit. We keep role-based access strict and can show the proof of actions.
02:37 Asha Patel: Latency and throughput — our main workload is inference for clinical summarization, about 200 QPS peak, many streaming responses but short sequences (512 tokens). We're sensitive to latency, but cost matters too.
02:48 Diego Rivera: For 200 QPS with short sequences, batching and KV cache help a lot. We'll map model choice and batching profile. Are you planning to run a private quantized model or a full fp16 model?
02:59 Sofia Ruiz: We're exploring a mixture: heavy models for accuracy (FP16) and some quantized variants for batch inference. Also want to run evals to check regression.
03:09 Diego Rivera: Good approach. We recommend starting with FP16 on A100s for initial rollouts, then experiment with q4f16 or 4bit quant for cost-sensitive endpoints. Our Optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles per workload.
03:23 Leo Martin: Any constraints around NVLink? We want to use it for model parallel but we also have single-root designs in one rack and cross-rack is limited.
03:32 Diego Rivera: We can operate in single-rack NVLink mode; cross-rack model parallelism is more complex and latency-sensitive. For your single-rack A100s we can do low-latency serving. If cross-rack is needed we recommend optimizing model shards and testing in a poc.
03:48 Ben Holmes: Data retention: logs and telemetry must be retained for 7 years and we need deletion controls for PII.
03:55 Maya Chen: We can configure retention windows, and our Private deployment supports retention policies and scrub/removal workflows triggered by your policies.
04:04 Asha Patel: Can you summarize the offline upgrade cadence? We can't accept weekly pushes; quarterly with emergency patch windows is our plan.
04:12 Diego Rivera: Typical cadence is quarterly for feature releases, monthly for security patches; for air-gapped customers we can lock cadence to quarterly and define emergency patch SLAs. All updates will be signed and go through your approval process.
04:28 Leo Martin: How about dependencies — CUDA, drivers? We manage container runtime but if you need specific driver versions we can ship compatible bundles; however kernel-level updates are on our side or on customer side?
04:40 Diego Rivera: Kernel-level and physical host OS patches are customer responsibility; our runtime runs in containers and we validate tested driver versions. We'll provide the tested matrix.
04:52 Asha Patel: What about FIPS and HSM? We need FIPS-validated crypto and HSM-backed key management.
04:58 Diego Rivera: We can integrate with FIPS HSMs and provide FIPS-compliant build options. We'll need to validate specific HSM vendors — you mentioned Thales earlier?
05:07 Ben Holmes: Yes, we have Thales Luna in production.
05:10 Diego Rivera: Great — we've integrated with Luna in prior deployments, will note that as a requirement.
05:16 Maya Chen: Are there any procurement or legal constraints we should know about?
05:20 Asha Patel: Our procurement requires a security questionnaire (we have a standard one), proof of SOC2 Type II, and a BAA for PHI — we're handling clinical data.
05:29 Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC2 and we can share evidence and the compliance pack. We also support BAA. I'll attach the security pack.
05:36 Leo Martin: For pilot sizing: how quickly could we stand up a 4-GPU test cluster for benchmarks? We want to run latency and throughput tests in two weeks if possible.
05:45 Diego Rivera: We can provide a pilot image and step-by-step air-gapped install doc; with your infra team we usually stand up a 4xA100 pilot in a week-ish if approvals are quick. We'll plan for a two-week turnaround including benchmarks.
05:58 Asha Patel: Success criteria for pilot: <=200ms p95 on short sequences, ability to process 200 QPS with batching, signed offline update flow validated, and audit log snapshots available.
06:10 Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll capture those as next steps. Any other blockers?
06:14 Sofia Ruiz: Just one — do you support canary rollouts in an air-gapped setup? We need to test model rollouts safely.
06:21 Diego Rivera: Yes, canary and staged rollouts are supported. The controller orchestrates rollouts internally and we can restrict traffic splits locally.
06:30 Ben Holmes: One more on data exfil: can you guarantee no outbound telemetry by default?
06:34 Diego Rivera: Defaults can be no outbound. We enable telemetry only if you opt in; for air-gapped we provide local collectors and offline export packages.
06:44 Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with the architecture doc, pricing, and SE deep dive for next week.
06:50 Asha Patel: thanks all.
06:52 Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll send notes and action items. Bye.
06:55 [call ends]
